name: Rezi
subcategory: resumes, job tracking and interview practice
tagline: Build ATS-friendly resume variants from a verified evidence bank and export PDF

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 resume; 1 AI interview; 3 PDF downloads lifetime; unlimited cover and resignation letters.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited resumes, AI interviews and PDF downloads; 1 human resume review per month.

tiers.name: Lifetime
tiers.limits: One-time $149 purchase; unlimited resumes, AI interviews and PDF downloads.
tiers.notes: Not a recurring plan; the monthly human-review allowance is excluded.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Up to 200 users per $99 monthly block; Pro features plus enterprise administration.
tiers.notes: Pricing is per 200-user block, not per individual seat.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 resume, 1 AI interview and 3 PDF downloads lifetime; cover and resignation letters are unlimited
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only for Pro/Enterprise + $149 one-time Lifetime license; no annual plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra human resume reviews start at $8; Free and Lifetime do not include the Pro plan's 1 review per month.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Rezi, build ATS-friendly resume variants from a verified evidence bank and export PDF. The hard boundary is templates, scoring, ai workflow, document rendering, and hosted convenience, plus data, distribution, and coaching.
coreLoopDIY: Build ATS-friendly resume variants from a verified evidence bank, tailor them to a supplied role, keep every claim traceable to the user's own evidence, and export PDF.
whatYouLose: templates, scoring, AI workflow, document rendering, and hosted convenience
ongoingBurden: document parsing, truthful claim handling, job-source changes, browser automation rules, privacy, model drift, and user review
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Rezi because people pay for convenience, curated guidance, and distribution; the personal tracking and drafting loop is highly buildable. The recurring cost buys document parsing, truthful claim handling, job-source changes, browser automation rules, privacy, model drift, and user review, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal job-search workspace DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Rezi in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and an optional OpenAI API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build ATS-friendly resume variants from a verified evidence bank, tailor them to a supplied role, keep every claim traceable to the user's own evidence, and export PDF.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a structured evidence bank for roles, projects, skills, dates, metrics, and source notes.
Import a job description and highlight requirements without inventing missing experience.
Generate a tailored resume variant only from approved evidence and show the source for each bullet.
Add application stages, contacts, tasks, dates, notes, documents, and a follow-up view.
Provide interview-question practice with answer notes and a self-review rubric, not deceptive live assistance.
Export resume data as JSON and PDF plus the application tracker as CSV.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mass application.
Deliberately leave out fabricated qualifications or deceptive interview assistance.
Deliberately leave out proprietary recruiter databases and guaranteed job outcomes.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
